English: What triage is, and your role
What is it?

Triage comes from hospital emergency rooms: patients are seen in order of danger, not in order of arrival. Cyber triage does the same with incidents. A ₹500 debit that is happening now is more urgent than a ₹2 lakh loss from last month, because the first can still be stopped. A Community Cyber First Responder is the first trained person a citizen meets. Their job is to identify what is happening, stabilise it, preserve what matters and route the case to the agency that can act — and to stay with it until the hand-over is confirmed.

At a community help desk, Mr Rao arrives first: he lost ₹2 lakh in an investment scam three weeks ago. Five minutes later Sunita arrives: her phone lost signal this morning and ₹18,400 has just been debited. A trained responder apologises to Mr Rao, helps Sunita call her bank and 1930 immediately, and then returns to Mr Rao's case, which still needs a complaint the same day. Lesson: urgency follows present danger and active loss. Both cases matter; one cannot wait.

What is it?

The four-colour urgency scale
What is it?

The urgency colour tells everyone how fast to act and what to do first. It is decided by present danger, active loss and spread. A colour is always written with a reason (“AMBER: second debit during intake; possible SIM takeover”). When a material fact changes, the colour is re-graded and the new reason recorded.

Stabilise safely
What is it?

Stabilising means stopping the harm from getting worse while keeping evidence intact. Most stabilising actions are simple: end the call, stop payments, call the bank from a clean phone, cut the network connection of a device that may be controlled remotely. The mistakes that destroy evidence — resetting, uninstalling, deleting chats — are also the ones frightened people try first.

Records, consent and hand-over
What is it?

A case is not finished when the citizen leaves; it is finished when the right agency has accepted it and the next check is scheduled. The record is short, factual and time-ordered, and it never contains secrets. Keep the citizen's identity off shared groups and dashboards.
